gen-dafont-eraser-fs-neco: Neco is a serif, swelling modestly from hairline to stem. Eraser does bold curves with no thinning at all; Neco does a mild, worn-felt-marker swell that never pinches shut.
gen-dafont-eraser-fs-recia: Cut-cord roundness: Eraser's bold letters have no thick or thin, while Recia, a text serif, has stems barely thicker than its joins. Give Eraser the bigger sizes, Recia the smaller.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-fs-gambetta: Industrial and plain, Hammerhead draws every stroke without contrast. What sets the pair apart is Gambetta, a text serif whose stroke weight shifts just enough to notice where bowls curve around.
gen-dafont-minecraftia-fs-bespoke-slab: Minecraftia sets chunky stems against connectors thin as a lightbulb filament, one character per beat. Bespoke Slab stays grounded and refined, giving tall bodies to every lowercase form, a sturdy foil to that fun.
gen-dafont-neuropol-fs-gambetta: Sealed, digital shapes: Neuropol closes its letters up tight, with just a slim channel to spare. Gambetta, a serif, then opens wide channels into each counter, so the page moves from locked to loose.
gen-dafont-neuropol-lora: Slim, digital outlines: Neuropol holds one thickness in every direction, whatever way the stroke runs. Lora then lets long reading flow, its strokes varying only slightly and its curves opening broadly.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-lora: Lora is a text serif, thinning modestly to hairlines at its curves. Oldtimer earns its keep big and short, its round forms like open parentheses and its strokes steady as a drawn string.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads bookish and graceful, a text serif whose stroke widths shift just enough to be noticed around each bowl. Shrink Over There and its constant-ink stripe starts to fade.
gen-dafont-over-there-lora: Fixed-nib stripes of ink: Over There follows a single thread. Over There excels at that plain, spaced-out stripe of ink, while Lora, a text serif, does medium contrast without sharp hairlines.
gen-fs-new-title-noto-serif: Noto Serif reads literary, with crossbars finer than its stems. New Title does the bold work, tall lowercase locked together like links in a fine chain, while Noto Serif keeps a subtle rhythm.
